role.altitude: The producer or director keeps every creative decision: shots, actors, the gallery and the research angle; breakdowns, shot-list typing, take logging and archive searching shrink.
skills_to_grow: Confirming drafted breakdowns scene by scene instead of writing them
role.ambitious_version: A director who walks into rehearsal with every scene broken down and every good take findable by timecode.

tasks.short: Break down the script per scene, look at locations, plan framing, composition and camera movement with the director of photography, write the shot list, plan sound and actor movement, and share the plan with the crew.

steps.what: Director reads the script and breaks down each scene: locations, characters, props and sound needs

loop.input: The shooting script with scene headings.
loop.output: Per scene: location, time of day, characters, props, sound and effects needs.
loop.check: Every element must quote the script line it comes from, or it is dropped. The director reads each scene's elements against the lines: is the element really needed on screen as the line means it; the director confirms each scene before it is used.
loop.stop: One pass per script version; stop when every scene is confirmed.
loop.why_not_simpler: Scene headings are structured, but props and sound needs sit in free action lines.

steps.what: Director visits locations and studies the space for each scene
Director plans framing, composition and camera movement for each shot with the director of photography
Director draws storyboards and writes the shot list
Director plans sound and actor movement for each scene with the sound designer
Director e-mails the shot list and storyboards to the crew

tasks.design: A production planning tool ({PROJECT}) holds the script; a bounded step drafts the scene breakdown with every element quoting its script line, and the director confirms scene by scene. The shot list is kept in the same tool, linked to scenes, so it reaches the crew and the call sheets without separate mails. Location visits, shot decisions with the director of photography, storyboards and blocking stay with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Breakdowns were typed from the script and shot lists sent as attachments that went out of date.
tasks.enabler_now: Production tools link scripts, breakdowns, shot lists and call sheets; script breakdown by a model is offered in beta.
tasks.still_hard: Every creative choice about the shot.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the scene in the space before the camera is there.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; the director starts planning with the breakdown done.

reach.learn: Whether confirmed breakdowns reduce schedule changes.

evidence.claim: A production tool offers call sheets, schedules and budgets, with AI script breakdown in beta since October 2025.
Language models can list props, characters and locations from screenplay text with the source line for each.

assumptions: Boundary: from the shooting script to the crew briefed; scheduling and booking crew are outside.
Input contract for s1: the shooting script in a screenplay format with scene headings; fallback is a manual breakdown.
Crew have access to the planning tool; freelancers get read access for the production.

Location visits, shot planning and blocking keep their full time. Storyboards and the shot list keep 90: they are the director's own work, and only retyping scene details goes. The shot list is the director's own save in the shared tool, so it has no separate approval.
unknowns: Whether the assistant director or the director makes the breakdown today.
research_questions: How many breakdown elements does the director correct per scene?
Do crew questions before the shoot fall?

already_counted.description: Director confirms or corrects each drafted scene breakdown.

incremental.description: Director keeps the shot list current in the tool when scenes change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a short film with few scenes, and crew still asking for the list by mail (s1 90, s6 60) (5.0); high: a series with many scenes and revisions (10.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare character notes, talk through the approach with actors, rehearse each scene, give notes between takes and send follow-up notes.

steps.what: Director prepares notes on approach and characterization for each scene
Director communicates the approach and characterization to actors in read-throughs and talks
Director rehearses each scene with the actors, setting movement and timing
Director gives actors notes between takes
Director writes follow-up notes to each actor after the day: typed today; from the day's voice memos after the change

loop.input: The director's own voice memos recorded during the day.
loop.output: A transcript split into notes per actor, by name.
loop.check: Every note must come from a memo passage with its time, or it is dropped. The director reads each actor's notes against the memo: it says what was meant, in the director's words, and nothing meant for one actor goes to another; unclear notes are rewritten.
loop.why_not_simpler: Typing up memos is the slow part, and speech has no fixed structure.

steps.what: Director reads each actor's notes before sending: right actor, right scenes, said the way the director would say it
Director sends the checked notes to each actor

approvals.approved_version: Each actor's notes exactly as checked by the director in s5b, sent once to that actor; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: Almost nothing changes: talking with actors, rehearsing and giving notes between takes stay with the director. Only the follow-up notes change: the director records voice memos during the day, and a bounded step turns them into notes per actor, each tied to a memo passage, which the director edits, reads once more and sends personally.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nothing blocked it; the work is people work.
tasks.enabler_now: Speech-to-text turns voice memos into text good enough to edit.
tasks.still_hard: Everything in the room: trust, timing and getting the take.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the one sentence that makes an actor understand the scene.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the director's week beyond less typing at night.

reach.learn: Whether notes from voice memos keep the director's tone.

evidence.claim: Speech-to-text tools transcribe voice memos into editable text.

assumptions: Boundary: from preparing character notes to follow-up notes sent; casting is outside.
Input contract for s5: voice memos the director records on a phone; fallback is typing.
Only the director's own memos are transcribed, not rehearsals or actors.
Read-throughs, rehearsals and notes between takes keep their full time.
unknowns: How often the director sends written notes.
research_questions: Does the director keep using memos after the first week?

already_counted.description: Director edits the drafted actor notes.

incremental.description: Director records voice memos during the day.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a stage production where notes are mostly given in person (s5 90) (0.3); high: a long shoot with written notes to many actors (3.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare the running order, rehearse, direct live broadcasts, films and recordings from the gallery or set, log takes, review the recording with the editor, sign off the final programme and hand it to playout.

steps.what: Director prepares the running order or shooting order with timings with the producer
Director rehearses with presenters, performers and camera crew
Director directs live broadcasts, films and recordings: calls shots, cues presenters and keeps time
Director marks good takes and notes timecodes and issues on paper during recording
Director reviews the recording and gives the editor notes for the cut
Director watches the final cut and signs off the final programme file for broadcast
Playout operator schedules and broadcasts the signed-off programme

approvals.approved_version: final programme file signed off in s6, identified by file name and checksum; any re-export voids it

tasks.design: The running order is kept in the gallery's rundown system ({OTHER}), which sums item timings instead of a spreadsheet. During recording the recording system logs every take with its actual timecode, and the director only taps good or bad and a short note on a tablet, so the editor gets a take log without retyping. Rehearsing, directing and reviewing stay with the director; playout broadcasts only the file version the director signed off.
tasks.previous_blocker: Take logs were written on paper and typed up or read aloud to the editor.
tasks.enabler_now: Recording systems expose takes and timecodes; tablet logging apps attach marks to them.
tasks.still_hard: Calling shots live and keeping a show on time.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the shot in the half second it matters.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; the director spends less time on logs after recording.

reach.learn: Whether timecoded good-take marks shorten the first assembly.

evidence.claim: Recording and logging systems attach take marks and notes to the actual timecode of each take.

assumptions: Boundary: from the running order to the programme handed to playout; editing itself is outside.
Input contract for s4: take start and end timecodes from the recording system; good or bad marks and notes from the director's tablet; fallback is the paper log.
The take log holds actual timecodes from the recorder, not the planned running order times.
For live broadcasts s6 and s7 do not apply; the broadcast is the direction in s3.
Rehearsal, directing and review keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of live versus recorded productions.
Whether the studio's recorder exposes take data.
research_questions: How much faster does the editor find takes with the log?

already_counted.description: Director marks takes and adds short notes on the tablet.

incremental.description: Director keeps the rundown template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly live shows with little logging (s1 95, s4 80) (2.3); high: recorded productions with many takes (8.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define research questions, search the internet and literature, search the video archive for footage, check rights, talk to experts and write the research file.

steps.what: Producer defines the research questions for the production topic
Producer researches the topic using the internet, articles and books

loop.input: One research question and the sources retrieved for it.
loop.output: A short answer with each fact tied to a source link and the quoted passage.
loop.check: Every fact must quote a passage found in the linked source, or it is dropped. The producer opens the source for every fact used on screen and checks that the passage supports the fact as stated, with its date and context.
loop.stop: One answer per question and source set.
loop.why_not_simpler: Search returns pages; the producer needs the facts pulled out with their source.

steps.what: Producer searches video archives for usable footage
Producer checks rights for the footage and asks rights holders for third-party clips
Producer calls experts and sources for background
Producer writes the research file for the director and editors

tasks.design: An answer step pulls facts from retrieved sources with quoted passages and links, and the producer opens every source used on screen. The video archive ({OTHER}) is searchable on transcripts and descriptions made when items are ingested, and shows the rights record with each item, so the producer asks rights holders only for third-party clips. Calls with experts stay with the producer, and a research file template collects facts, clips with timecodes and rights status for the producer to summarise.
tasks.previous_blocker: Archive footage could only be found by title and description, and facts were copied from pages by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Speech-to-text indexes archive footage; language models pull facts with checkable quotes.
tasks.still_hard: Judging which source is reliable and which clip tells the story.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the expert or clip nobody else used.
tasks.altitude: The producer spends research time on sources and experts instead of searching; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Which searches transcripts answer that descriptions did not.

evidence.claim: Language models can answer a question from retrieved sources and quote the passages, so each fact can be checked.
Text and data mining of online content is allowed unless the rightholder reserved it by machine-readable means.
Using archive footage in a programme needs a licence from the rightholder regardless of how it was found.

assumptions: Boundary: from research questions to the research file; scripting and editing are outside.
Input contract for s3: archive transcripts and descriptions made at ingest by the archive team; rights records kept by the archive per item; fallback is title search.
Coverage: about 60% of the archive has transcripts; s3 is priced at that share.
s4 is part of obtaining rights to footage, which sibling task 27-2012.00:22538 covers; its saving is counted there, so s4 keeps its full time here.
unknowns: How much of the archive is transcribed.
Share of footage from third parties.
research_questions: How many facts from the answer step fail the producer's source check?
How much faster are clips found with transcript search?

already_counted.description: Producer opens sources for facts used on screen.

incremental.description: Producer keeps a list of trusted sources and the research file template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a topic with little archive footage and mostly expert calls (s2 85, s3 90) (10.0); high: a history or current-affairs programme with many archive items (23.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
